_README: Copy this to the report folder as manual.json and fill it in from the worksheet
fetch_macro.py printed. Delete any block you did not look up -- an omitted figure
is listed honestly in macro_pack.md section 6, whereas a guessed one is not.
EVERY entry needs three things or build_pack.py refuses it:
value   the number, unitless (units come from the registry)
period  WHAT IT OBSERVES, not today. YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM or YYYY.
A June-2026 CPI print entered in August is period 2026-06.
An Indian FISCAL year uses its END month: FY26 is 2026-03, never 2026.
A period in the future is refused (IMF WEO forecasts excepted).
source  the citation string, matching the `cite` format in the worksheet
Keys under `figures` must exist in scripts/registry.py. Inventing a key here is
rejected on purpose: two spellings of the same figure fragment the shared store
in reports/_knowledge/ and kb.py stops recalling it.
_WEO_README: Fill the `weo` block ONLY when the vintage gate blocked the mirror -- that is the
route back in for figures read by hand off imf.org. If fetch_macro.py wrote WEO
figures successfully, delete the whole block; anything here overrides the fetch.
`vintage` is the edition, YYYY-MM, and it becomes the citation for every figure in
the block: 'IMF WEO 2026-04'. 'IMF WEO' with no month is not a source.
Geographies: world, advanced, emde, euro, us, china, japan, india.
Subjects: gdp, cpi, gdp_usd, gdp_pc, cad, govt_debt.
Years are WEO periods. India is FISCAL year: WEO 2026 = FY27.

india_10y_gsec.note: must reconcile with risk_free in assumptions.json

india_wpi.source: Office of the Economic Adviser, WPI release, <Month Year>

india_gdp_fy_actual.source: MoSPI, Provisional Estimates of Annual GDP, <Month Year>
india_gdp_fy_actual.note: state the FY in the report text, e.g. FY26

india_gdp_latest_q.source: MoSPI, Quarterly Estimates of GDP, Q<n> FY<yy>
india_gdp_latest_q.note: period = the last month of the quarter observed

industry.label: <segment> domestic volumes, FY26
industry.note: SIAM is wholesale despatches; FADA is retail registrations. Say which.

industry.label: <industry> India market size
industry.note: forecast_year is mandatory for any market-size figure
